title.zh: 卷七十二 列傳第二: 宗室 義宗倍 章肅皇帝李胡 順宗濬 晉王敖盧斡
title.en: Volume 72 Biographies 2: Imperial Family: Yi Zongbei, the Foreign Emperor Zhang Su, Shun Zongjun, Jin Wangaoluwo
title.raw: 卷七十二 列傳第二: 宗室 義宗倍 章肅皇帝李胡 順宗濬 晉王敖盧斡 Volume 72 Biographies 2: Imperial Family: Yi Zongbei, the Foreign Emperor Zhang Su, Shun Zongjun, Jin Wangaoluwo

sentences.zh: ○義宗倍

translations.literal: ○ Yizong Bei
translations.idiomatic: Yizong Bei

sentences.zh: 〈（子平王隆先晉王道隱）〉

translations.literal: (Sons: Prince of Ping Longxian and Prince of Jin Daoyin)
translations.idiomatic: (Sons: Prince of Ping Longxian and Prince of Jin Daoyin)

sentences.zh: 章肅皇帝李胡

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangsu Li Hu
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangsu Li Hu

sentences.zh: 〈（子宋王喜隱）〉

translations.literal: (Son: Prince of Song Xiyin)
translations.idiomatic: (Son: Prince of Song Xiyin)

sentences.zh: 順宗濬晉王敖盧斡

translations.literal: Shunzong Jun; Prince of Jin Aolugan
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong Jun and Prince of Jin Aolugan

sentences.zh: 義宗，名倍，小字圖欲，太祖長子，母淳欽皇后蕭氏。

translations.literal: Yizong, personal name Bei, childhood name Tuyu, eldest son of Taizu, mother Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong, whose personal name was Bei and childhood name Tuyu, was Taizu's eldest son; his mother was Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏好學，外寬內摯。

translations.literal: In youth clever and eager to learn; outwardly lenient, inwardly earnest.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick-witted and studious, mild in manner yet ardent at heart.

sentences.zh: 神冊元年春，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Shence, he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Shence year 1 (916) he was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時太祖問侍臣曰：「受命之君，當事天敬神。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu asked his attending ministers, saying: "A ruler who has received the Mandate should serve Heaven and revere the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu asked his ministers, "A ruler who has received Heaven's mandate ought to honor Heaven and the spirits.

sentences.zh: 有大功德者，朕欲祀之，何先？」

translations.literal: Among those of great merit and virtue, whom does Your Majesty wish to sacrifice to first?"
translations.idiomatic: Among the figures of greatest merit, whom should I worship first?"

sentences.zh: 皆以佛對。

translations.literal: All answered with the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: They all named the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「佛非中國教。」

translations.literal: Taizu said: "Buddhism is not the teaching of the Central States."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "Buddhism is not a teaching native to China."

sentences.zh: 倍曰：「孔子大聖，萬世所尊，宜先。」

translations.literal: Bei said: "Confucius the great sage, honored for ten thousand generations, should come first."
translations.idiomatic: Bei replied, "Confucius is the supreme sage, revered through the ages—he should come first."

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，即建孔子廟，詔皇太子春秋釋奠。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased, immediately built a temple to Confucius, and decreed that the crown prince perform the spring and autumn sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted, had a Confucian temple built at once, and ordered the crown prince to conduct the spring and autumn rites of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 嘗從征烏古、党項，為先鋒都統，及經略燕地。

translations.literal: He once followed campaigns against the Wugu and Tangut, served as vanguard commander-in-chief, and directed operations in the Yan region.
translations.idiomatic: He once campaigned against the Wugu and Tangut as vanguard commander-in-chief and directed operations in the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 太祖西征，留倍守京師，因陳取渤海計。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned west, he left Bei to guard the capital and presented a plan for taking Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched west, he left Bei to guard the capital and urged a plan to conquer Bohai.

sentences.zh: 天顯元年，從征渤海。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxian he followed the campaign against Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxian year 1 he joined the expedition against Bohai.

sentences.zh: 拔扶餘城，上欲括戶口，倍諫曰：「今始得地而料民，民必不安。

translations.literal: Fuyu city was taken; the sovereign wished to register households, and Bei remonstrated, saying, "Having just gained the land and now counting the people, the people are sure to be unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: After Fuyu city fell the emperor wished to register households; Bei remonstrated, "Having just taken the land, a census will unsettle the people.

sentences.zh: 若乘破竹之勢，徑造忽汗城，克之必矣。」

translations.literal: If we ride the momentum of splitting bamboo and strike straight for Hohan city, we are certain to take it."
translations.idiomatic: If we press the advantage like splitting bamboo and march straight on Hohan city, we are sure to take it."

sentences.zh: 太祖從之。

translations.literal: Taizu followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 倍與大元帥德光為前鋒，夜圍忽汗城，大諲譔窮蹙，請降。

translations.literal: Bei and the Great Marshal Deguang served as vanguard; they besieged Hohan city by night, and Dayinzan, hard pressed, begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Bei and Great Marshal Deguang led the vanguard and besieged Hohan city by night; Dayinzan, cornered, offered surrender.

sentences.zh: 尋復叛，太祖破之。

translations.literal: Soon he rebelled again, and Taizu defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon rebelled again, and Taizu put him down.

sentences.zh: 改其國曰東丹，名其城曰天福，以倍為人皇王主之。

translations.literal: Its state was renamed Eastern Dan, its city renamed Tianfu, and Bei was made Human Emperor King to rule it.
translations.idiomatic: The state was renamed Eastern Dan, the city renamed Tianfu, and Bei was installed as Human Emperor King to rule it.

sentences.zh: 仍賜天子冠服，建元甘露，稱制，置左右大次四相及百官，一用漢法。

translations.literal: He was further granted the cap and robes of the Son of Heaven, adopted the era name Ganlu, exercised regency, and established left and right great secondary halls, four chancellors, and the hundred offices—all following Han institutions.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted imperial cap and robes, adopted the era name Ganlu, ruled in his own right, and set up left and right great secondary halls, four chancellors, and the full bureaucracy—all on the Han model.

sentences.zh: 歲貢布十五萬端，馬千匹。

translations.literal: Each year he rendered tribute of one hundred fifty thousand bolts of cloth and one thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he paid tribute of one hundred fifty thousand bolts of cloth and one thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「此地瀕海，非可久居，留汝撫治，以見朕愛民之心。」

translations.literal: The sovereign instructed him, saying, "This land borders the sea and cannot be long occupied; I leave you to govern and soothe it, that my love for the people may be seen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "This land lies on the sea and cannot be held long; I leave you to govern it and show my care for the people."

sentences.zh: 駕將還，倍作歌以獻。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to return, Bei composed a song and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to return, Bei composed a song and presented it.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，太祖曰：「得汝治東土，吾復何憂。」

translations.literal: Taking leave at the steps, Taizu said, "With you governing the eastern lands, what further worry have I?"
translations.idiomatic: As he took leave at court, Taizu said, "With you governing the east, what have I left to fear?"

sentences.zh: 倍號泣而出。

translations.literal: Bei wailed and wept as he went out.
translations.idiomatic: Bei wept aloud as he departed.

sentences.zh: 遂如儀坤州。

translations.literal: He then proceeded to Yikun Prefecture as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: He then went on to Yikun Prefecture as ordered.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸部多叛，大元帥討平之。

translations.literal: Before long many tribes rebelled; the Great Marshal suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long many tribes rebelled; the Great Marshal put them down.

sentences.zh: 太祖訃至，倍即日奔赴山陵。

translations.literal: When Taizu's death notice arrived, Bei set out that same day to hurry to the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When word of Taizu's death arrived, Bei set out the same day for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 倍知皇太后意欲立德光，乃謂公卿曰：「大元帥功德及人神，中外攸屬，宜主社稷。」

translations.literal: Bei knew the Empress Dowager wished to install Deguang, and therefore said to the dukes and ministers: "The Great Marshal's merit reaches men and spirits; within and without all look to him—he should hold the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the Empress Dowager meant to elevate Deguang, Bei told the chief ministers, "The Great Marshal's achievements touch both men and spirits; court and country alike look to him—he ought to rule the realm."

sentences.zh: 乃與群臣請於太后而讓位焉。

translations.literal: He then joined the officials in petitioning the Empress Dowager and yielded the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He and the officials petitioned the Empress Dowager, and he yielded the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是大元帥即皇帝位，是為太宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Great Marshal assumed the imperial position—this was Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Marshal then took the throne as Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 太宗既立，見疑，以東平為南京，徙倍居之，盡遷其民。

translations.literal: Once Taizong was established, Bei came under suspicion; Dongping was made the Southern Capital, Bei was moved to dwell there, and all its people were relocated.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession Bei fell under suspicion; Dongping was made the Southern Capital, Bei was relocated there, and the entire population was moved away.

sentences.zh: 又置衛士陰伺動靜。

translations.literal: Guards were also posted to watch his movements in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Guards were also set to spy on his movements in secret.

sentences.zh: 倍既歸國，命王繼遠撰《建南京碑》，起書樓於西宮，作《樂田園詩》。

translations.literal: After Bei returned to his domain, he ordered Wang Jiyuan to compose the "Stele on Building the Southern Capital," raised a book tower in the Western Palace, and wrote the poem "Joy in the Garden."
translations.idiomatic: Once back in his domain, Bei had Wang Jiyuan draft the "Stele on Building the Southern Capital," built a book tower in the Western Palace, and composed "Joy in the Garden."

sentences.zh: 唐明宗聞之，遣人跨海持書密召倍。

translations.literal: Tang Emperor Mingzong heard of this and sent men across the sea with a letter to summon Bei in secret.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Emperor Mingzong heard of it, he sent envoys across the sea with a secret letter inviting Bei.

sentences.zh: 倍因畋海上。

translations.literal: Bei happened to be hunting on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Bei happened to be hunting at sea.

sentences.zh: 使再至，倍謂左右曰：「我以天下讓主上，今反見疑；

translations.literal: When the envoys came a second time, Bei said to those beside him: "I yielded the realm to our lord; now I am met with suspicion instead;
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys came again, Bei told his attendants, "I gave the empire to our sovereign, yet now I am distrusted;

sentences.zh: 不如適他國，以成吳太伯之名。」

translations.literal: better to go to another state and fulfill the name of Wu Taibo."
translations.idiomatic: better to go abroad and earn a name like Wu Taibo's."

sentences.zh: 立木海上，刻詩曰：「小山壓大山，大山全無力。

translations.literal: He set up a post on the sea and carved a poem: "A little hill presses the great hill; the great hill is wholly without strength.
translations.idiomatic: He erected a post on the sea and carved a poem: "A little hill weighs on the great hill—the great hill has no strength at all.

sentences.zh: 羞見故鄉人，從此投外國。」

translations.literal: Ashamed to face the people of my homeland, from this I cast myself to a foreign land."
translations.idiomatic: Too ashamed to face the folk of home—from this I go to a foreign land."

sentences.zh: 攜高美人，載書浮海而去。

translations.literal: Taking Lady Gao the fair, he loaded his books and went off across the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Taking Lady Gao with him, he loaded his books and sailed away across the sea.

sentences.zh: 唐以天子儀衛迎倍，倍坐船殿，眾官陪列上壽。

translations.literal: Tang received Bei with the ceremonial guard of the Son of Heaven; Bei sat in the boat-palace while officials stood in attendance offering longevity wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Tang received Bei with imperial ceremonial guard; he sat in the boat-palace while officials stood in attendance offering congratulations.

sentences.zh: 至汴，見明宗。

translations.literal: Reaching Bian, he met Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Bian he was received by Emperor Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 明宗以莊宗后夏氏妻之，賜姓東丹，名之曰慕華。

translations.literal: Mingzong gave him in marriage Empress Xia of Zhuangzong and granted the surname Eastern Dan, naming him Muhua.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong gave him Zhuangzong's consort, Lady Xia, in marriage and granted the surname Eastern Dan, naming him Muhua.

sentences.zh: 改瑞州為懷化軍，拜懷化軍節度使、瑞慎等州觀察使。

translations.literal: Ruizhou was changed to Huaihua Army; he was appointed military commissioner of Huaihua Army and surveillance commissioner of Ruizhou, Shen, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizhou was made Huaihua Army, and he was appointed military commissioner of Huaihua Army and surveillance commissioner of Ruizhou, Shen, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 復賜姓李，名贊華。

translations.literal: He was again granted the surname Li and named Zanhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was again granted the surname Li and named Zanhua.

sentences.zh: 移鎮滑州，遙領虔州節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Huazhou and held concurrently the post of military commissioner of Qianzhou in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Huazhou and concurrently held the post of military commissioner of Qianzhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 倍雖在異國，常思其親，問安之使不絕。

translations.literal: Though Bei was in a foreign land, he constantly thought of his kin, and envoys sending inquiries after their welfare never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Though abroad, Bei never ceased thinking of his family, and messengers sending greetings home never stopped.

sentences.zh: 後明宗養子從珂弒其君自立，倍密報太宗曰：「從珂弒君，盍討之。」

translations.literal: Later Mingzong's adopted son Congke murdered his sovereign and seized the throne; Bei secretly reported to Taizong, saying, "Congke murdered his lord—why not punish him?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Mingzong's adopted son Congke murdered his sovereign and seized power; Bei secretly informed Taizong, "Congke has murdered his lord—we ought to punish him."

sentences.zh: 及太宗立石敬瑭為晉主，加兵於洛。

translations.literal: When Taizong installed Shi Jingtang as Jin sovereign and added troops at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong set up Shi Jingtang as Jin emperor and sent additional troops against Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 從珂欲自焚，召倍與俱，倍不從，遣壯士李彥紳害之，時年三十八。

translations.literal: Congke wished to burn himself, summoned Bei to join him, and Bei refused; he sent the strong man Li Yanzhen to kill him—he was thirty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: Congke meant to burn himself and summoned Bei to die with him; Bei refused, and Congke sent the strongman Li Yanzhen to kill him. Bei was thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 有一僧為收瘞之。

translations.literal: A monk gathered and buried his remains.
translations.idiomatic: A monk gathered and buried his remains.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭入洛，喪服臨哭，以王禮權厝。

translations.literal: Jingtang entered Luoyang, came in mourning garb to weep before the coffin, and provisionally interred him with the rites due a king.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingtang entered Luoyang he came in mourning to weep at the coffin and provisionally interred Bei with royal rites.

sentences.zh: 後太宗改葬於醫巫閭山，謚曰文武元皇王。

translations.literal: Later Taizong reburied him on Mount Yiwulü and posthumously titled him King Yuanhuang the Civil and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizong had him reburied on Mount Yiwulü and posthumously styled him King Yuanhuang the Civil and Martial.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，謚讓國皇帝，陵曰顯陵。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was posthumously titled Emperor Who Yielded the Realm; his tomb was called Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded, Bei was posthumously styled Emperor Who Yielded the Realm; his tomb was named Xianling.

sentences.zh: 統和中，更謚文獻。

translations.literal: During Tonghe his title was changed to Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tonghe era his posthumous title was changed to Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十年，增謚文獻欽義皇帝，廟號義宗，及謚二后曰端順，曰柔貞。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Chongxi his honorific was advanced to Emperor Wenxian, Qinyi; his temple name was Yizong, and the two empresses were posthumously titled Duanshun and Rouzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongxi year 20 his honorific was advanced to Emperor Wenxian, Qinyi; his temple name was Yizong, and his two consorts were posthumously styled Duanshun and Rouzhen.

sentences.zh: 倍初市書至萬卷，藏於醫巫閭絕頂之望海堂。

translations.literal: Bei at first bought books until they reached ten thousand scrolls, storing them in the Wanghai Hall atop the summit of Mount Yiwulü.
translations.idiomatic: Bei had once bought books until his collection reached ten thousand scrolls, which he kept in the Wanghai Hall on the summit of Mount Yiwulü.

sentences.zh: 通陰陽，知音律，精醫藥、砭焫之術。

translations.literal: He mastered yin and yang, understood music and pitch, and was expert in medicine and the arts of acupuncture and moxibustion.
translations.idiomatic: He understood yin and yang, knew music and pitch, and was skilled in medicine, acupuncture, and moxibustion.

sentences.zh: 工遼、漢文章，嘗譯《陰符經》。

translations.literal: He was accomplished in Khitan and Han writing and once translated the "Classic of the Hidden Talisman."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well in both Khitan and Chinese and once translated the "Classic of the Hidden Talisman."

sentences.zh: 善畫本國人物，如《射騎》、《獵雪騎》、《千鹿圖》，皆入宋秘府。

translations.literal: He was skilled at painting figures of his own country, such as "Mounted Archers," "Hunting Snow Cavalry," and "A Thousand Deer"—all entered the Song imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at painting Khitan subjects; works such as "Mounted Archers," "Hunting Snow Cavalry," and "A Thousand Deer" all entered the Song imperial collection.

sentences.zh: 然性刻急好殺，婢妾微過，常加刲灼。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was harsh and impatient and he loved killing; for slight faults in maidservants and concubines he often applied branding and cautery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was harsh and quick-tempered and prone to cruelty; for the slightest slip by maids or concubines he often branded or cauterized them.

sentences.zh: 夏氏懼而求削髮為尼。

translations.literal: Lady Xia, in fear, begged to shave her head and become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xia, terrified, begged to shave her head and take vows as a nun.

sentences.zh: 五子：長世宗，次婁國、稍、隆先、道隱，各有傳。

translations.literal: Five sons: the eldest Shizong, next Louguo, Shao, Longxian, and Daoyin—each has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: the eldest was Shizong, followed by Louguo, Shao, Longxian, and Daoyin—each treated in his own biography.

sentences.zh: 平王隆先，字團隱，母大氏。

translations.literal: Prince of Ping Longxian, style Tuanyin, mother the Da clan.
translations.idiomatic: Longxian, Prince of Ping, whose style was Tuanyin, was born to the Da clan.

sentences.zh: 景宗即位，始封平王。

translations.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Ping.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong succeeded he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Ping.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼政事令，留守東京。

translations.literal: Before long he concurrently served as chief of governmental affairs and remained to guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made chief of governmental affairs while also serving as regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 薄賦稅，省刑獄，恤鰥寡，數薦賢能之士。

translations.literal: He lightened taxes, reduced penal cases, cared for widowers and widows, and repeatedly recommended worthy and capable men.
translations.idiomatic: He eased taxes, reduced penal cases, cared for the widowed and orphaned, and repeatedly recommended able men.

sentences.zh: 後與統軍耶律室魯同討高麗有功，還薨，葬醫巫閭山之道隱谷。

translations.literal: Later he campaigned against Goryeo together with army commander Yelu Shilu with merit; returning, he died, and was buried in Daoyin Valley on Mount Yiwulü.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined army commander Yelu Shilu in a successful campaign against Goryeo; on his return he died and was buried in Daoyin Valley on Mount Yiwulü.

sentences.zh: 平王為人聰明，博學能詩，有《閬苑集》行於世。

translations.literal: Prince of Ping was clever by nature, broadly learned and skilled in poetry; his "Collection of the Lang Garden" circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ping was clever, broadly learned, and skilled in poetry; his Collection of the Lang Garden circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 保寧之季，其子陳哥與渤海官屬謀殺其父，舉兵作亂，上命轘裂於市。

translations.literal: Late in Baoning his son Chenge plotted with Bohai officials to kill his father, raised troops in rebellion, and the sovereign ordered him torn apart by carriages in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Baoning era his son Chenge plotted with Bohai officials to murder him and rose in rebellion; the emperor ordered Chenge executed by dismemberment in the market.

sentences.zh: 晉王道隱，字留隱，母高氏。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Daoyin, style Liuyin, mother the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyin, Prince of Jin, whose style was Liuyin, was born to the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 道隱生於唐，人皇王遭李從珂之害，時年尚幼，洛陽僧匿而養之，因名道隱。

translations.literal: Daoyin was born in Tang; when the Human Emperor King met harm at the hands of Li Congke he was still young, and a Luoyang monk hid and raised him—hence the name Daoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyin was born in Tang; when the Human Emperor King was killed by Li Congke he was still a child, and a Luoyang monk hid and raised him—hence the name Daoyin.

sentences.zh: 太宗滅唐，還京，詔賜外羅山地居焉。

translations.literal: When Taizong destroyed Tang and returned to the capital, an edict granted him land on Mount Wailuo to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong destroyed Tang and returned to the capital, an edict granted him residence on Mount Wailuo.

sentences.zh: 性沈靜，有文武才，時人稱之。

translations.literal: His nature was calm and reserved; he had civil and military talent, and men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Calm and reserved by nature, he had both civil and military talent, and contemporaries praised him.

sentences.zh: 景宗即位，封蜀王，為上京留守。

translations.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and made regent of the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong succeeded he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and appointed regent of the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 乾亨元年，遷守南京，號令嚴肅，民獲安業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianheng he was transferred to guard the Southern Capital; his orders were stern and disciplined, and the people found security in their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianheng year 1 he was transferred to guard the Southern Capital; his rule was strict and orderly, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 居數年，徙封荊王。

translations.literal: After several years he was moved to the enfeoffment of Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After several years his title was changed to Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 統和初，病薨，追封晉王。

translations.literal: Early in Tonghe he died of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tonghe era he died of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自古新造之國，一傳而太子讓，豈易得哉？

translations.literal: The commentary says: Since antiquity in newly founded states, for the crown prince to yield in a single transmission—how easily is that attained?
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In newly founded states since antiquity, how rare it is for a crown prince to yield the throne in the very first succession!

sentences.zh: 遼之義宗，可謂盛矣！

translations.literal: Liao's Yizong may be called magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Liao's Yizong stands among the finest examples!

sentences.zh: 然讓而見疑，豈不兆於建元稱制之際乎？

translations.literal: Yet after yielding he met with suspicion—was this not foreshadowed at the time he established an era name and exercised regency?
translations.idiomatic: Yet once he had yielded he was distrusted—was that not already foreshadowed when he adopted an era name and ruled in his own right?

sentences.zh: 斯則一時君臣昧於禮制之過也。

translations.literal: This was a fault of ruler and ministers of that age, blind to ritual and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: That was a lapse of ruler and ministers alike, who failed to grasp proper ritual and institutions.

sentences.zh: 束書浮海，寄跡他國，思親不忘，問安不絕，其心甚有足諒者焉。

translations.literal: Bundling his books and crossing the sea, lodging his footsteps in another state, he did not forget his kin and never ceased sending inquiries after their welfare—his heart has much that may be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: He packed his books and crossed the sea to live abroad, yet never forgot his family and kept sending greetings home—there is much in his heart that deserves understanding.

sentences.zh: 觀其始慕泰伯之賢而為遠適之謀，終疾陳恒之惡而有請討之舉，誌趣之卓，蓋已見於早歲先祀孔子之言歟。

translations.literal: Observe how at first he admired Taibo's virtue and made plans for distant departure, and at the end detested Chen Heng's wickedness and urged a punitive campaign—his lofty aims were already seen in his early years in the words that put Confucius first in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: See how early on he admired Taibo's virtue and planned exile abroad, and in the end loathed Chen Heng's crime and urged his ruler to punish it—his high purpose was already plain in youth, when he argued to honor Confucius first.

sentences.zh: 善不令終，天道難詰，得非性卞嗜殺之所致也？

translations.literal: Goodness did not bring him a peaceful end; Heaven's way is hard to question—was it not caused by a harsh nature and love of killing?
translations.idiomatic: Virtue did not win him a gentle end; Heaven's ways are hard to fathom—was it not his harsh, bloodthirsty temper that brought it about?

sentences.zh: 雖然，終遼之代，賢聖繼統，皆其子孫。

translations.literal: Even so, through the whole Liao age, worthy and sage rulers succeeded one another—all were his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, through the entire Liao dynasty the worthy and sage who held the throne were all his descendants.

sentences.zh: 至德之報，昭然在茲矣。

translations.literal: The reward of supreme virtue is manifest here.
translations.idiomatic: The reward of supreme virtue shines plainly in this.

sentences.zh: 章肅皇帝，小字李胡，一名洪古，字奚隱，太祖第三子，母淳欽皇后蕭氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangsu, childhood name Li Hu, another name Honggu, style Xiyin, third son of Taizu, mother Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangsu, childhood name Li Hu, also called Honggu, style Xiyin, was Taizu's third son; his mother was Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.

sentences.zh: 少勇悍多力，而性殘酷，小怒輒黥人面，或投水火中。

translations.literal: In youth brave, fierce, and strong, yet cruel by nature; at a slight anger he would tattoo faces or cast people into water or fire.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was fierce and powerful, but cruel by nature; the least provocation could bring facial tattooing or being thrown into water or fire.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗觀諸子寢，李胡縮項臥內，曰：「是必在諸子下。」

translations.literal: Taizu once watched his sons sleep; Li Hu lay inside with neck drawn in, and said: "This one is sure to rank below the other sons."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once watched his sons sleep. Li Hu lay curled up with his neck drawn in, and Taizu said, "This one will surely rank below his brothers."

sentences.zh: 又嘗大寒，命三子采薪。

translations.literal: On another occasion in severe cold he ordered the three sons to gather firewood.
translations.idiomatic: On another bitterly cold day he ordered the three sons to gather firewood.

sentences.zh: 太宗不擇而取，最先至；

translations.literal: Taizong took without choosing and arrived first;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong gathered without picking and came back first;

sentences.zh: 人皇王取其乾者束而歸，後至；

translations.literal: the Human Emperor King took the dry pieces, bound them, and returned, arriving later;
translations.idiomatic: the Human Emperor King chose the dry wood, bound it into a bundle, and returned later;

sentences.zh: 李胡取少而棄多，既至，袖手而立。

translations.literal: Li Hu took little and discarded much; when he arrived he stood with hands in sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu took little and threw away much; when he arrived he stood with empty hands in his sleeves.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「長巧而次成，少不及矣。」

translations.literal: Taizu said: "The eldest is clever, the second accomplishes; the youngest does not measure up."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "The eldest is clever, the second gets things done; the youngest falls short."

sentences.zh: 而母篤愛李胡。

translations.literal: Yet the mother dearly loved Li Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his mother doted on Li Hu.

sentences.zh: 天顯五年，遣徇地代北，攻寰州，多俘而還，遂立為皇太弟，兼天下兵馬大元帥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxian he was sent to traverse the land north of Dai, attacked Huan Prefecture, took many captives and returned, and was then installed as Imperial Younger Brother Heir and concurrently Great Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxian year 5 he was sent to campaign in the Dai north, attacked Huan Prefecture, returned with many captives, and was made Imperial Younger Brother Heir while also serving as commander-in-chief of all forces.

sentences.zh: 太宗親征，常留守京師。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned in person, he regularly remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizong led campaigns in person, Li Hu usually stayed behind as regent in the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位鎮陽，太后怒，遣李胡將兵擊之。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne at Zhenyang, the Empress Dowager was angry and sent Li Hu to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong assumed the throne at Zhenyang, the Empress Dowager in anger sent Li Hu with an army against him.

sentences.zh: 至泰德泉，為安端、留哥所敗。

translations.literal: Reaching Taidé Spring, he was defeated by Anduan and Liuge.
translations.idiomatic: At Taidé Spring he was defeated by Anduan and Liuge.

sentences.zh: 太后與世宗隔潢河而陣，各言舉兵意。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and Shizong faced each other across the Huang River in battle array, each stating the reason for raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager and Shizong drew up on opposite banks of the Huang River and each explained why he had taken up arms.

sentences.zh: 耶律屋質入諫太后曰：「主上已立，宜許之。」

translations.literal: Yelü Wuzhi entered and remonstrated with the Empress Dowager, saying: "The sovereign is already established—you should acknowledge him."
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Wuzhi went in and urged the Empress Dowager, "The emperor is already enthroned—you ought to accept him."

sentences.zh: 時李胡在側，作色曰：「我在，兀欲安得立？」

translations.literal: At that time Li Hu was at her side; he changed color and said: "While I am here, how can Wuyue be established?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu stood at her side, flushed with anger, and said, "As long as I live, how can Wuyue take the throne?"

sentences.zh: 屋質曰：「奈公酷暴失人心何！」

translations.literal: Wuzhi said: "What of it that you, sir, are cruel and violent and have lost the people's hearts!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi replied, "What can be done when you are cruel and violent and have lost the people's hearts?"

sentences.zh: 太后顧李胡曰：「昔我與太祖愛汝異於諸子，諺云：『偏憐之子不保業，難得之婦不主家。』

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager turned to Li Hu and said: "In the past I and Taizu loved you differently from the other sons. A proverb says: 'A child over-favored cannot keep the estate; a wife hard to win does not manage the household.'
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager turned to Li Hu and said, "Taizu and I once loved you more than your brothers. As the proverb runs, 'The child too fondly indulged cannot keep the estate; the wife too hard won cannot keep the house.'

sentences.zh: 我非不欲立汝，汝自不能矣。」

translations.literal: It is not that I did not wish to install you—you yourself could not do it."
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I would not make you emperor—you simply could not hold it."

sentences.zh: 及會議，世宗使解劍而言。

translations.literal: When they met in council, Shizong had his sword removed before he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: At the council Shizong had his sword taken before he addressed them.

sentences.zh: 和約既定，趨上京。

translations.literal: Once the peace pact was fixed, they hurried to the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace was agreed, they hurried to the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 會有告李胡與太后謀廢立者，徙李胡祖州，禁其出入。

translations.literal: Soon someone reported that Li Hu and the Empress Dowager plotted deposition and installation; Li Hu was moved to Zuzhou and his coming and going forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Li Hu and the Empress Dowager were plotting to depose the emperor, Li Hu was exiled to Zuzhou and forbidden to leave.

sentences.zh: 穆宗時，其子喜隱謀反，辭逮李胡，囚之，死獄中，年五十，葬玉峰山西谷。

translations.literal: In Muzong's time his son Xiyin plotted rebellion; testimony implicated Li Hu, who was imprisoned and died in jail at age fifty, buried in the western valley of Mount Yufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Muzong his son Xiyin rebelled; testimony implicated Li Hu, who was imprisoned and died in jail at fifty, and was buried in the western valley of Mount Yufeng.

sentences.zh: 統和中，追謚欽順皇帝。

translations.literal: During Tonghe he was posthumously titled Emperor Qinshun.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tonghe era he was posthumously styled Emperor Qinshun.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十一年，更謚章肅，后曰和敬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi the title was changed to Zhangsu; the consort was called Hejing.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongxi year 21 his title was changed to Zhangsu; his consort was styled Hejing.

sentences.zh: 二子：宋王喜隱、衛王宛。

translations.literal: Two sons: Prince of Song Xiyin and Prince of Wei Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Prince of Song Xiyin and Prince of Wei Wan.

sentences.zh: 喜隱，字完德，雄偉善騎射，封趙王。

translations.literal: Xiyin, style Wande, imposing and skilled in mounted archery, was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyin, whose style was Wande, was imposing and skilled in mounted archery and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 應歷中，謀反，事覺，上臨問有狀，以親釋之。

translations.literal: During Yingli he plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered the sovereign questioned him in person and found the facts established, yet released him because of kinship.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yingli era he plotted rebellion; when the plot was exposed the emperor questioned him in person, found the charge proved, yet released him as a kinsman.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復反，下獄。

translations.literal: Before long he rebelled again and was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he rebelled again and was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 景宗即位，聞有赦，自去其械而朝。

translations.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, hearing there was an amnesty, he removed his own fetters and came to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong succeeded, hearing that an amnesty had been declared, he removed his own shackles and came to court.

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「汝罪人，何得擅離禁所！」

translations.literal: The sovereign in anger said, "You are a criminal—how dare you leave your place of confinement on your own!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said, "You are a convicted man—how dare you leave confinement on your own!"

sentences.zh: 詔誅守者，復置於獄。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the guards executed, and he was again placed in prison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the guards put to death, and he was returned to prison.

sentences.zh: 及改元保寧，乃宥之，妻以皇后之姊，復爵，王宋。

translations.literal: When the era was changed to Baoning he was pardoned, given in marriage the empress's elder sister, restored to rank, and enfeoffed as Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the era was changed to Baoning he was pardoned, married to the empress's elder sister, restored to rank, and enfeoffed as Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 喜隱輕僄無恒，小得志即驕。

translations.literal: Xiyin was frivolous and inconstant; with the slightest success he grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyin was frivolous and unreliable; the least success made him arrogant.

sentences.zh: 上嘗召，不時至，怒而鞭之，由是憤怨謀亂。

translations.literal: The sovereign once summoned him and he did not come promptly; in anger the sovereign flogged him, and from this he nursed resentment and plotted disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor summoned him he failed to come promptly; the emperor in anger had him flogged, and from then on he nursed resentment and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 貶而復召，適見上與劉繼元書，辭意卑遜，諫曰：「本朝於漢為祖，書旨如此，恐虧國體。」

translations.literal: Demoted yet summoned again, he happened to see the sovereign's letter to Liu Jiyuan, its wording humble and submissive, and remonstrated, saying, "Our dynasty is ancestor to Han—if the letter's intent is thus, I fear the dignity of the state will be impaired."
translations.idiomatic: Though demoted he was summoned again; seeing the emperor's letter to Liu Jiyuan, whose tone was abject, he remonstrated, "Our dynasty is ancestor to Han—with wording like this, the dignity of the state will suffer."

sentences.zh: 帝尋改之。

translations.literal: The emperor soon revised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon revised the letter.

sentences.zh: 授西南面招討使，命之河東索吐蕃戶，稍見進用。

translations.literal: He was appointed southwestern frontier pacification commissioner and ordered to the east of the Yellow River to seek out Tibetan households; he gradually came into favor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed southwestern frontier pacification commissioner and sent east of the river to seek out Tibetan households; he gradually won greater favor.

sentences.zh: 復誘群小謀叛，上命械其手足，築圜土，囚祖州。

translations.literal: He again enticed petty men to plot rebellion; the sovereign ordered his hands and feet shackled, a round-walled enclosure built, and him imprisoned at Zuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again incited petty followers to rebel; the emperor ordered his limbs shackled, a round-walled cell built, and him imprisoned at Zuzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋降卒二百餘人欲劫立喜隱，以城堅不得入，立其子留禮壽，上京留守除室擒之。

translations.literal: More than two hundred surrendered Song soldiers wished to seize and install Xiyin; unable to enter because the walls were strong, they installed his son Liulishou; Upper Capital regent Chushi captured him.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred surrendered Song soldiers tried to seize the city and install Xiyin; failing to enter because the walls were strong, they installed his son Liulishou instead; Upper Capital regent Chushi captured him.

sentences.zh: 留禮壽伏誅，賜喜隱死。

translations.literal: Liulishou was executed, and Xiyin was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Liulishou was put to death, and Xiyin was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 論曰：李胡殘酷驕盈，太祖知其不才而不能教，太后不知其惡而溺愛之。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Li Hu was cruel and arrogant; Taizu knew he lacked talent yet could not instruct him, and the Empress Dowager did not know his wickedness and doted on him.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Li Hu was cruel and arrogant. Taizu knew he lacked talent but could not teach him; the Empress Dowager did not see his wickedness and spoiled him.

sentences.zh: 初以屋質之言定立世宗，而復謀廢立。

translations.literal: At first through Wuzhi's words Shizong's enthronement was settled, yet they again plotted deposition and installation.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wuzhi's counsel secured Shizong's enthronement, yet mother and son plotted deposition again.

sentences.zh: 子孫繼以逆誅，並及其身，可哀也已。

translations.literal: Descendants in succession met execution for treason, reaching even to his person—pitiable indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants were executed one after another for treason, and ruin reached him as well—a lamentable end.

sentences.zh: 夫自太祖之世，剌葛、安端首倡禍亂，太祖既不之誅，又復用之，固為有君人之量，然惟太祖之才足以駕馭，庶乎其可也。

translations.literal: From Taizu's age, Cige and Anduan first raised calamity and disorder; Taizu neither punished them to the full, yet employed them again—this truly showed the measure of a ruler of men, yet only Taizu's talent could rein them in; perhaps that could suffice.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu's reign Cige and Anduan were the first to stir rebellion; Taizu neither executed them outright nor cast them off permanently, which showed true magnanimity as a ruler—yet only Taizu's ability could keep them in hand, and even that was barely enough.

sentences.zh: 李胡而下，宗王反側，無代無之，遼之內難，與國始終。

translations.literal: From Li Hu downward, imperial princes were restless; no reign lacked this—Liao's internal troubles ran with the state from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: From Li Hu onward, imperial princes were forever restless; no reign was free of it—Liao's internal strife dogged the dynasty from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 厥後嗣君，雖嚴法以繩之，卒不可止。

translations.literal: Later successor rulers, though they bound them with stern law, ultimately could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Later emperors bound them with harsh law, yet still could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 烏乎，創業垂統之主，所以貽厥孫謀者，可不審歟！

translations.literal: Alas! A founding ruler who hands down the succession—what he bequeaths to his descendants' plans: can it go unexamined!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! Founders who establish a dynasty and pass it on—what they leave their heirs demands the utmost care!

sentences.zh: 順宗，名濬，小字耶魯斡，道宗長子，母宣懿皇后蕭氏。

translations.literal: Shunzong, personal name Jun, childhood name Yeluwo, eldest son of Daozong, mother Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong, whose personal name was Jun and childhood name Yeluwo, was Daozong's eldest son; his mother was Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan.

sentences.zh: 幼而能言，好學知書。

translations.literal: As a child he could speak; he loved learning and knew books.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he could speak early, loved learning, and was well read.

sentences.zh: 道宗嘗曰：「此子聰慧，殆天授歟！」

translations.literal: Daozong once said, "This child is clever—perhaps Heaven bestowed it!"
translations.idiomatic: Daozong once said, "This boy is clever—perhaps Heaven itself bestowed it!"

sentences.zh: 六歲，封梁王。

translations.literal: At age six he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At six he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 明年，從上獵，矢連發三中。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the sovereign on a hunt and with arrows in swift succession hit three times.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined the emperor on a hunt and with three arrows in swift succession scored three hits.

sentences.zh: 上顧左右曰：「朕祖宗以來，騎射絕人，威震天下。

translations.literal: The sovereign turned to those beside him and said, "From my ancestors onward, horsemanship and archery have been unmatched and awe has shaken the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "Since my ancestors, our horsemanship and archery have been unmatched and our might has shaken the realm.

sentences.zh: 是兒雖幼，不墜其風。」

translations.literal: Though this boy is young, he does not fall short of that tradition."
translations.idiomatic: Though this boy is young, he does not fall short of that tradition."

sentences.zh: 後遇十鹿，射獲其九。

translations.literal: Later encountering ten deer, he shot and took nine.
translations.idiomatic: Later, meeting ten deer, he brought down nine.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，設宴。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and held a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor held a banquet.

sentences.zh: 八歲，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: At age eight he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 大康元年，兼領北南樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dakang he concurrently directed the affairs of the Northern and Southern Bureaus of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Dakang year 1 he also took charge of the Northern and Southern Bureaus of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及母后被害，太子有憂色。

translations.literal: When the empress mother was murdered, the crown prince wore a troubled look.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress mother was killed, the crown prince's face showed deep worry.

sentences.zh: 耶律乙辛為北院樞密使，常不自安。

translations.literal: Yelü Yixin served as Northern Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was often ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yixin, Northern Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was constantly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 會護衛蕭忽古謀害乙辛，事覺，下獄。

translations.literal: It happened that guard Xiao Hugu plotted to kill Yixin; the affair was discovered and he was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: When guard Xiao Hugu plotted to kill Yixin, the plot was exposed and he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 副點檢蕭十三謂乙辛曰：「臣民心屬太子，公非閥閱，一日若立，吾輩措身何地！」

translations.literal: Deputy Inspector Xiao Shisan said to Yixin: "Officials and people look to the crown prince; you, sir, are not of noble pedigree—if he ascends one day, where shall we place ourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Inspector Xiao Shisan told Yixin, "Officials and commoners alike look to the crown prince. You are not of high birth—once he reigns, where will men like us stand?"

sentences.zh: 乃與同知北院宣徽事蕭特裏特謀構陷太子，陰令右護衛太保耶律查剌誣告都宮使耶律撒剌、知院蕭速撒、護衛蕭忽古謀廢立。

translations.literal: He then joined Associate Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Palace Attendants Xiao Telite in plotting to frame the crown prince, secretly ordering Right Guard Commissioner Yelü Chala to accuse falsely Palace Director Yelü Sala, Commissioner Xiao Susa, and guard Xiao Hugu of plotting deposition and installation.
translations.idiomatic: He and Associate Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Palace Attendants Xiao Telite then plotted to frame the crown prince, secretly ordering Right Guard Commissioner Yelü Chala to accuse Palace Director Yelü Sala, Commissioner Xiao Susa, and guard Xiao Hugu of plotting a coup.

sentences.zh: 詔案無跡，不治。

translations.literal: An imperial order investigated and found no trace; the case was not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial inquiry found no evidence, and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 乙辛復令牌印郎君蕭訛都斡等言：「查剌前告非妄，臣實與謀，欲殺耶律乙辛等，然後立太子。

translations.literal: Yixin again ordered Seal and Insignia Attendant Xiao Eduogan and others to say: "Chala's earlier accusation was not false; I truly joined the plot, intending to kill Yelü Yixin and the rest, and then install the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin then had Seal and Insignia Attendant Xiao Eduogan and others declare, "Chala's first report was true—I was in the plot to kill Yelü Yixin and his faction, then put the crown prince on the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣若不言，恐事發連坐。」

translations.literal: If your servant does not speak, I fear that when the affair breaks out I will be implicated by association."
translations.idiomatic: If I do not confess now, I fear I will be punished when the plot is uncovered."

sentences.zh: 帝信之，幽太子於別室，以耶律燕哥鞫案。

translations.literal: The emperor believed it, confined the crown prince in a separate chamber, and had Yelü Yange conduct the inquest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed them, confined the crown prince in a separate room, and put Yelü Yange in charge of the investigation.

sentences.zh: 太子具陳枉狀曰：「吾為儲副，尚何所求。

translations.literal: The crown prince fully stated the injustice of the case, saying: "I am heir apparent—what more could I seek?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince laid out the injustice of the charge: "I am heir apparent—what more could I want?

sentences.zh: 公當為我辨之。」

translations.literal: You, sir, ought to clear me."
translations.idiomatic: You must speak for me."

sentences.zh: 燕哥乃乙辛之黨，易其言為款伏。

translations.literal: Yange was of Yixin's faction and altered his words into a confession.
translations.idiomatic: Yange was Yixin's man and twisted his words into a confession.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，廢太子為庶人。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and deposed the crown prince to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and deposed the crown prince to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 將出，曰：「我何罪至是！」

translations.literal: As he was about to go out, he said: "What crime of mine reaches this!"
translations.idiomatic: As he was led out he cried, "What crime have I committed to deserve this!"

sentences.zh: 十三叱登車，遣衛士闔其扉。

translations.literal: Shisan shouted at him to mount the carriage and sent guards to shut the doors.
translations.idiomatic: Shisan shouted at him to get in the carriage and had guards slam the doors shut.

sentences.zh: 徙於上京，囚圜堵中。

translations.literal: He was moved to the Upper Capital and imprisoned within a round enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to the Upper Capital and held in a round-walled cell.

sentences.zh: 乙辛尋遣達魯古、撒八往害之，太子年方二十，上京留守蕭撻得紿以疾薨聞。

translations.literal: Yixin soon sent Dalugu and Saba to go and harm him; the crown prince was only twenty years old; the Upper Capital regent Xiao Tade was deceived with a report that he had died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin soon sent Dalugu and Saba to kill him. The crown prince was only twenty; Upper Capital regent Xiao Tade was tricked with a report that he had died of illness.

sentences.zh: 上哀之，命有司葬龍門山。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him and ordered the authorities to bury him at Longmen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved and ordered an official burial at Longmen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 欲召其妃，乙辛陰遣人殺之。

translations.literal: He wished to summon the crown prince's consort; Yixin secretly sent men to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: When he wished to summon the crown prince's consort, Yixin secretly had her murdered.

sentences.zh: 帝後知其冤，悔恨無及，謚曰昭懷太子，以天子禮改葬玉峰山。

translations.literal: Later the emperor learned of his injustice; regret came too late. He was posthumously titled Crown Prince Zhaohuai and reburied at Mount Yufeng with rites due an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later learned of the injustice, remorse came too late. He posthumously styled him Crown Prince Zhaohuai and reburied him on Mount Yufeng with imperial rites.

sentences.zh: 乾統初，追尊大孝順聖皇帝，廟號順宗，妃蕭氏貞順皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qian Tong he was posthumously honored as Emperor the Great Filial and Shun the Sage; temple name Shunzong; consort of the Xiao clan, Empress Zhenshun.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qian Tong era he was posthumously elevated to Emperor the Great Filial and Shun the Sage, with temple name Shunzong; his consort of the Xiao clan was styled Empress Zhenshun.

sentences.zh: 一子，延禧，即天祚皇帝。

translations.literal: One son, Yanxi—that is, Emperor Tianzuo.
translations.idiomatic: He had one son, Yanxi, who became Emperor Tianzuo.

sentences.zh: 論曰：道宗知太子之賢，而不能辨乙辛之詐，竟絕父子之親，為萬世惜。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Daozong knew the crown prince's worth yet could not discern Yixin's fraud, and in the end severed father-son kin—a thing for ten thousand generations to lament.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Daozong knew his son's worth yet could not see through Yixin's deceit, and in the end destroyed the bond between father and son—a loss the ages lament.

sentences.zh: 乙辛知為一身之計，不知有君臣之義，豈復知有太子乎！

translations.literal: Yixin knew only schemes for his own person and did not know the righteousness between ruler and minister—how could he still know there was a crown prince!
translations.idiomatic: Yixin cared only for himself and knew nothing of the duty between ruler and minister—how could he spare a thought for the crown prince!

sentences.zh: 奸邪之臣亂人家國如此，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Wicked and treacherous ministers throw households and states into disorder like this—can one fail to take warning!
translations.idiomatic: When treacherous ministers can overturn a household and a realm like this, who would not take warning!

sentences.zh: 可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Can one fail to take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Who would not take warning!

sentences.zh: 晉王，小字敖盧斡，天祚皇帝長子，母曰文妃蕭氏。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin, childhood name Aolugan, eldest son of Emperor Tianzuo, mother called Literary Consort of the Xiao clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, childhood name Aolugan, was Emperor Tianzuo's eldest son; his mother was Literary Consort of the Xiao clan.

sentences.zh: 甫髫齔，馳馬善射。

translations.literal: While still in childhood he galloped horses and was skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: While still a child he rode hard and shot well.

sentences.zh: 出為大丞相耶律隆運後，封晉王。

translations.literal: Having been given out as heir to Grand Chancellor Yelu Longyun, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Having been made heir to Grand Chancellor Yelu Longyun, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 性樂道人善，而矜人不能。

translations.literal: By nature he delighted in praising others' goodness and was forbearing toward those who lacked ability.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he delighted in praising others' goodness and was forbearing toward those who lacked ability.

sentences.zh: 時宮中見讀書者輒斥，敖盧斡嘗入寢殿，見小底茶剌閱書，因取觀。

translations.literal: At the time anyone seen reading in the palace was rebuked; Aolugan once entered the sleeping hall, saw the junior attendant Chacha reading a book, and took it to look.
translations.idiomatic: At the time anyone caught reading in the palace was scolded; Aolugan once entered the sleeping quarters, saw junior attendant Chacha reading, and took the book to look.

sentences.zh: 會諸王至，陰袖而歸之，曰：「勿令他人見也。」

translations.literal: When the princes arrived he secretly tucked it in his sleeve and returned it, saying, "Do not let others see it."
translations.idiomatic: When other princes arrived he quietly slipped it back into his sleeve and returned it, saying, "Do not let anyone else see this."

sentences.zh: 一時號稱長者。

translations.literal: For a time he was acclaimed as a man of mature character.
translations.idiomatic: For a time he was acclaimed as a man of mature character.

sentences.zh: 及長，積有人望，內外歸心。

translations.literal: When he grew up he accumulated public esteem, and within and without all turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he won wide esteem, and court and country alike looked to him.

sentences.zh: 保大元年，南軍都統耶律余睹與其母文妃密謀立之，事覺，余睹降金，文妃伏誅，敖盧斡實不與謀，免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoda, Southern Army commander-in-chief Yelu Yudu and Aolugan's mother Literary Consort secretly plotted to install him; when the affair was discovered Yudu surrendered to Jin, Literary Consort was executed, and Aolugan had in truth not joined the plot and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoda year 1 Southern Army commander-in-chief Yelu Yudu and Aolugan's mother Literary Consort secretly plotted to put him on the throne; when the plot was exposed Yudu defected to Jin, Literary Consort was executed, and Aolugan, who had not joined the plot, was spared.

sentences.zh: 二年，耶律撒八等復謀立，不克。

translations.literal: In the second year Yelu Saba and others again plotted to install him and did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Yelu Saba and others again plotted to enthrone him but failed.

sentences.zh: 上知敖盧斡得人心，不忍加誅，令縊殺之。

translations.literal: The sovereign knew Aolugan had won the people's hearts and could not bear to punish him directly, and ordered him strangled.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Aolugan had won the people's hearts and unable to bear executing him openly, the emperor ordered him strangled.

sentences.zh: 或勸之亡，敖盧斡曰：「安忍為蕞爾之軀，而失臣子之大節！」

translations.literal: Some urged him to flee; Aolugan said, "How could I bear to save this petty body and lose the great integrity of subject and son!"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to flee; Aolugan said, "How could I save this petty life and betray the great duty of subject and son!"

sentences.zh: 遂就死。

translations.literal: He then accepted death.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to his death.

sentences.zh: 聞者傷之。

translations.literal: Those who heard of it grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 論曰：天祚不君，臣下謀立其子，適以殺之。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Tianzuo did not act as ruler; his ministers plotted to install his son, and thereby brought about his death.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Tianzuo failed as a ruler; his ministers plotted to put his son on the throne—and thereby brought about the son's death.

sentences.zh: 敖盧斡重君父之命，不亡而死，申生其恭矣乎！

translations.literal: Aolugan honored the command of ruler and father, not fleeing yet dying—was he not as dutiful as Shen Sheng!
translations.idiomatic: Aolugan honored his sovereign and father, refusing flight though it meant death—was he not as dutiful as Prince Sheng of Jin!
